name: AgentOS TUI Oriented System
source: user request: TUI oriented AgentOS; previous workflow final audit
goal: Turn AgentOS from a runtime-and-ecosystem Alpha with demo/projection TUI into a TUI-oriented operating system where the terminal console is the primary durable operator surface for AgentCore runs, approvals, recovery, audit, support and ecosystem lifecycle.
core_thesis: TUI is the OS operator surface, not a second runtime. It must control AgentCore and SecurityExecution through typed APIs, display durable projections, and never own planner, resolver, policy or side-effect logic.
non_goals: Do not make a GUI or web UI the primary surface.
Do not add arbitrary shell escape as a TUI feature.
Do not duplicate AgentCore, SecurityExecution, aom resolver or support bundle logic inside TUI.
Do not require network, external LLM, host package manager or Firecracker for baseline TUI operation.
Do not make TUI-only state authoritative over RunStore or AuditJournal.
primary_acceptance: Operator can submit an intent from TUI and see a durable AgentCore run projection.
Operator can advance safe read-only steps, approve/deny gated steps and recover interrupted runs through TUI commands.
TUI can explain why an action is blocked, paused, denied, rollback-pending or degraded.
TUI can project aom ecosystem state and create activation previews without activating by stage/install.
Boot/runtime packaging exposes TUI as the default operator console while preserving noninteractive smoke gates.
Release gates include TUI replay, production runbook smoke and QEMU console proof.
